title: Long delay echoes rise when Earth-Moon L5 is above the horizon

tellings.quote: And one study even found a statistically significant increase in LDEs when the Earth-Moon L5 Lagrange point was above the horizon.

plain: Long delay echoes are radio signals that come back seconds after they were sent, a puzzle dating to 1927, and Michels says one study found a "statistically significant increase" in them when the Earth-Moon L5 point was above the horizon. L5 is a Lagrange point, a spot in space where the pulls of the Earth and Moon balance so that an object can sit there stably. Michels tells it himself, without naming the study, as a hint that something could be parked at that point and returning the signals.
